decision: measured the laptop webcam before designing anything
why: needed real numbers on what is wrong with a weak webcam in bad light
result: 15 real fps in auto, 60 Hz anti-flicker in a 50 Hz country, soft picture, camera already denoises

decision: leading design is one WebGL2 shader core in TypeScript used by a web page, a browser extension and a desktop app
why: laptop has no C++/Rust/.NET compilers, browsers give camera capture and GPU on every OS for free, and only the virtual camera needs native code
result: to be confirmed by prototypes and research

decision: recorded 9 clips of the same scene under forced camera states (as found, 30 fps auto, 50 Hz, dim, dark, very dark, high gain, two colour casts)
why: same scene in good and bad states lets us score output against the best state instead of guessing
result: 9 clips, about 136 frames each, camera restored

decision: checked which camera controls Chrome exposes for this webcam
why: the web design only works if the browser can run its own exposure control
result: VERIFIED: manual exposure, gain (as exposureCompensation 1..8), colour temperature, brightness all settable; 1/32 s manual gives 30 real fps, 1/16 s gives 16

decision: kept the name Sunroom and the plan to both drive the camera and repair the picture
why: landscape research found no free cross-platform tool that does both automatically, and the name has no camera or video collision
result: gap confirmed; Zero-DCE and SCI licences rule them out for shipping

decision: scoring harness: exact camera frames, independent face boxes, same-scene reference, three naive baselines
why: every version must be judged before vs after on the same footage, not by eye alone
result: raw and baselines scored

decision: no neural network in version 1; classical GPU pipeline; history clamped by min/max; faces only lifted when below a healthy band
why: research found the well-known low-light models are non-commercial or unlicensed and too slow for integrated graphics
result: adopted

decision: v0: deflicker rows, motion-aware temporal denoise, guided-filter tone mapping anchored on the face
why: first full pass to see where it breaks
result: faces fixed on realistic clips; blue-cast clip turned to colour garbage; dark areas stayed noisy

decision: replaced SNR with noise in display units plus contrast-to-noise, and made colour error lightness-normalised
why: SNR rewarded the gamma baseline for flattening contrast, and raw colour distance punished correct brightening
result: fairer table

decision: v1: noise model per brightness band, spatial fill-in where history is thin, white balance capped with desaturation fallback, near-black colour drained
why: v0 pictures showed dark areas not accumulating and uncorrectable casts amplified
result: contrast-to-noise 52.8 vs raw 26.1 and gamma 27.9 on 6 realistic clips; dark noise 2.25 vs gamma 6.94; 10 to 18 ms per frame on Intel UHD

decision: did not register the virtual camera filter; stopped at the blocked step
why: the safety classifier refused the per-user registry write as persistence, and that is the owner's call to make
evidence: blocked PowerShell call in transcript; DLLs only downloaded to %LOCALAPPDATA%/sunroom/vcam
result: BLOCKED: per-user DirectShow registration is unproven until the owner allows the test

decision: desktop shell will be Electron, frames go out through koffi; browser extension uses MediaStreamTrackProcessor and Generator, never requestAnimationFrame
why: Tauri needs Rust and MSVC which this machine lacks; rAF freezes in background tabs
result: adopted

decision: live test on the real webcam from the as-found state: director pins the shutter and raises sensor gain
why: the web design only pays off if the app can undo the camera's frame-rate drop by itself
result: VERIFIED: 14.9 fps to 30 fps within 3 s, face luma about 106, 9 to 11 ms per frame, camera restored on stop

decision: added a gain ceiling with headroom check after seeing gain bounce 4 to 5 every second
why: raise and lower rules overlapped, so the loop cycled; clipped highlights cannot be recovered but a dark face can
result: gain settles at 4 and stays

decision: measured the denoiser alone: noise halves and banding drops about 80 percent with no detail loss, but stalls there
why: this camera's noise is correlated across frames, so averaging has a ceiling; added a spatial stage with a floor on assumed remaining noise
result: v3 crops visibly cleaner on the high-gain clip; temporal metric nearly unchanged, as expected for a spatial filter

decision: reverted to a wider plausible-skin range after colour errors rose in v3
why: the owner's correctly balanced skin measured R/G 1.4 to 1.6, outside the range I had taken from studio swatches
result: normal clips back to raw-level colour error (0.1 to 4)

decision: raised the white balance cap from 0.7 to 1.1 log units
why: the moderate cast clip needed 1.05 and was being stopped short
result: skin error 11.4 to 4.2 and shirt 19.8 to 2.7 on the warm clip; wall stays cyan (18): skin is fixed first, the rest of the scene is not

decision: scored with the shipped face detector instead of annotated boxes, and with no face input
why: annotated boxes are an advantage the live app does not have
result: detector on enhanced output found the face in 100 percent of checks on 8 of 9 clips and matched the annotated scores after the first second; with no face input the face only reaches luma 59 to 66

decision: 39 unit tests for meter, controller and director; broke two rules on purpose to confirm they fail
why: tests that pass with broken code prove nothing
result: both mutations caught

decision: accepted the web app after rerunning its end-to-end test myself and reading its screenshots
why: a builder's report is not evidence; the test output and pictures are
evidence: apps/web/test/e2e.mjs (16 checks passed on rerun), apps/web/test/shots/desktop.png
result: accepted; replaced the word stops in the status line with plain wording

decision: live run of the web app on the real webcam went wrong twice: the director pinned the shutter while the machine was busy, and leaving the page left the camera in manual exposure
why: found by running the real thing under load, not by the tests
evidence: eval/live-web.mjs output in transcript; camctl list showed Exposure flags 2 and Gain 2 afterwards
result: fixed: director ignores low frame rate when we are the bottleneck, starts from automatic exposure, and keeps a note of original gain and black level; camera restored by hand with camctl; clean live rerun still owed

decision: tried brightening limits of 4, 4.5 and 5.5 stops on the darkest clips and settled on 5
why: 5.5 looked grey and flat, 4 left the face at luma 52; no clean winner, so a middle value
evidence: data/crop_gaincap.jpg, data/out/final_compare.txt (4.5 run: face 62 on the high-gain clip)
result: set to 5; a judgment call, not a measured optimum

decision: ran Sunroom a second time over its own well-lit output
why: the claim that it leaves a good picture alone needed a test
result: not identity: 4.6 grey levels mean change, brightness 160.8 to 164.1, lift 0.24 stops, no colour change

decision: an enhancement failure now passes the camera straight through instead of ending the track
why: reading the extension code showed a mid-call GPU failure would have frozen someone's video
result: VERIFIED with a forced context loss: error reported, track live, 52 frames in 2.5 s afterwards

decision: reran final scoring with the 5-stop limit, annotated faces and shipped detector
why: numbers in the report must come from the shipped settings
result: cnr 26.1 raw, 27.9 gamma, 50.4 annotated, 51.2 detector; detector flicker 0.52 vs 0.03 looked like a regression

decision: checked whether the detector run pumps brightness or only settles at start
why: a steady wobble would be a real defect, a start-up ramp is not
evidence: wall mean over time, second half of each clip, three clips
result: start-up only: steady state 0.015 to 0.023 percent, same as annotated; the detector finds the face about a second in, and colour correction takes about 3 s to converge

decision: reran the desktop builder's tests myself and read its screenshots and code
why: a builder's report is not evidence
evidence: npm test -w apps/desktop, npm run e2e -w apps/desktop, apps/desktop/test/shots
result: sender test and e2e pass; 29.6 fps into the simulated filter, nothing read while no app listens; real filter in a real app still unproven

decision: ran the desktop app on the real webcam and found the director pinned the shutter at start for a camera that was fine
why: status said the camera fell to 4 fps; a probe showed the camera was at 30 and our cold start was the slow part
result: root cause: frame rate was measured from arrival times, which our own slowness drags down

decision: camera frame rate now comes from the browser's own frame counter, with a 2.5 s warm-up and arrival times only as fallback
why: the counter reports 29.7 fps while a deliberately slow reader takes 5, so our load cannot fake a slow camera
result: VERIFIED live: no pin at start, pinned only when the camera itself fell to 15, held 30, camera handed back on quit; web 16 checks, desktop e2e, failsafe pass

decision: the director now also takes over when the camera holds its frame rate but the face is starved of light
why: live frame showed a dim green face: camera sat at 30 fps and gain 1 while software lifted 5 to 6 stops; the run that used sensor gain looked far better
result: VERIFIED live: took over at 4.3 s, gain 1 to 6, face luma 70 to 106, 30 fps held, no flapping in 30 s, camera handed back; not taken when the shutter is short or highlights are near clipping

decision: reran the extension builder's test myself, read its screenshots and code, then changed three things
why: status text said stops, the face detector was attached by mutating core options, and the test defaulted to an Edge path that no longer exists
result: 13 of 13 pass on Chromium 153 headless; real call sites not tested

decision: Edge's Application folder vanished at 06:17 IST during the extension builder's run; checked what this session did
why: must rule out that our work removed a system browser
evidence: builder transcript commands (only temp-folder deletes and Playwright process stops), Program Files (x86)/Microsoft/Edge timestamps, EdgeCore/Optimized/Installer touched 06:17
result: not caused by this session as far as the evidence shows; msedge.exe still present under EdgeCore/156.0.4314.58; left untouched, flagged to the owner
